title: Town pets: Cat, Dog and Bunny licenses
player_outcome: Buy a Cat, Dog or Bunny License from the Zoologist and use it. A town pet moves into a free house, wanders the town, and can be petted.
design: TownNpcKind.Pet (from TownNpcDef.Pet = true). Pets: no shop or services; never count as residents; invulnerable and never targeted; need a valid house. BeginTalk on a pet opens a tiny dialog with a 'Pet' button, which plays the player's 'use' action and a heart burst particle, as in Terraria's petting.

New item behavior 'license' {flag} in ItemBehaviorSpecs, with its handler in a new ItemUseSystem.Town.cs. It sets the world flag 'license_<pet>'. If the flag is already set it is refused with 'This license has already been used.' through the Refused event.
Data data/town/pets.json: town_cat, town_dog, town_bunny with arrival [{flag license_cat}] etc. Items license_cat/dog/bunny (5 gold). The Zoologist shop entries are added in P5-17.

Models: a new tools/blender/bgen/pets.py quadruped generator (metaball body, head with ears and whiskers, tail, four legs; a small rig with walk/idle/sit/lie clips) for town_cat and town_dog. town_bunny reuses the 'bunny' generator at scale 1.4. If the art phase adds a better quadruped, reuse it.
TownRenderer: non-humanoid residents use CreatureVisual.Play('walk'/'idle'). Name tag e.g. 'Whiskers the Cat'.
data_changes: 3 town NPC defs, 3 items, reference concepts terraria:town_cat/dog/bunny and the licenses
tests: PetTests.LicenseSetsFlagOnce: the second use is refused and not consumed
PetTests.PetMovesIntoHouseAndDoesNotCount: ResidentCount unchanged after the cat arrives
verification: build_all --check; validate; dotnet test; smoke PASS
In game: buy a license, use it, build a house → the cat moves in and walks around
risks: TownNpc.HalfExtents is static for humans; pets use the humanoid nav agent, which is fine for 1-cell-wide doors. A per-def size is a follow-up.
